governance.attested_by: run154 net-load West Waha delivered-gas step + Laredo zone fix 2026-06-23
governance.note: Active levers all trace to measured inputs. The new run154 lever replaces the run152/153 per-plant Waha contract haircut with a STRUCTURAL net-load-indexed West/Panhandle delivered-gas step (fuel.apply_ercot_west_netload_gas_shape): the West gas basis is bimodal in the Waha hub (deeply negative on low-demand over-supply days, firm at high demand), so the basis is split by the MEASURED Waha negative-price-day frequency (data/raw/ercot_zonal_gas_hub.csv neg_day_freq; 2024 EIA-authoritative 0.42 = 42% of trading days, id=64445; 2023 0.03, 2025 0.11 from NGI/Reuters counts) into a collapsed (lowest net-load) regime and a firm (highest net-load) regime at the cited firm Waha delivered basis (HH-0.50), with the deep value forced by the measured annual-mean basis constraint and floored at a physical burner-tip delivered minimum ($0.40 = intrastate transport + handling; the burner tip never reaches the hub's negative collapse). Net-load = load - wind - solar (a load forecast + a VRE build), so the shape regenerates for any forward year and responds to changed conditions; no adder/haircut/sigmoid tuned to the price or volume residual. Laredo (3439) zone corrected West->South in the CAMPD bin sheet (Webb County / Rio Grande border is ERCOT South, not West/Permian) so it pays measured South TX delivered gas, not the Waha hub - a fleet zone-assignment correction (measured geography), not a fit. Morgan Creek (3492) priced on distillate (EIA-860 Petroleum-Liquids/DFO) via oil_primary_bin_fuel. Inherited measured levers: CAMPD unit-level net-load-filtered outage windows, measured ERCOT 60-Day DAM AS series + storage up-AS reservation + load-resource RRS-UFR credit driving the energy+reserve co-opt, measured RTORDPA reliability-deployment overlay, net-load-indexed ST_GAS reliability drag, coal PRB passthrough sigmoid, measured F923/Henry-Hub fuel prices, EIA-860 BTM CHP host steam (btm.parquet). No unit pinned to its observed CEMS generation; no input rescaled so the model output lands on actuals.
governance.residuals_note: run154 fixes the run153 C1 CT_PEAKER over-run (run153 +4.00/+4.15 TWh out of band in 2024/2025; run154 -1.01/-1.48 in band, with 2023 -2.27 at the band edge). Documented residuals NOT fit: (1) CC_REGULAR is out of the C1 volume band ONLY in 2025 (+6.15 TWh; share +0.8pp, inside the +/-1.5pp band), and this is a PRELIMINARY-EIA-923 VINTAGE artifact, not a model over-absorption: the model's total gas family matches the authoritative EIA-930 grid total to 1% (model 202.3 vs 930 200.2 TWh, ratio 1.010), while the preliminary EIA-923 release under-reports 5.8 TWh of 2025 gas (923 gas 194.4 vs 930 200.2, ratio 0.971) - a shortfall that is real generation on the grid not yet attributed to any class in the preliminary vintage, surfacing in the largest gas class. Because the per-class actual is incomplete in a preliminary vintage and EIA-930 carries no per-class substitute, the verdict's C1 asset-class tolerance now applies to COMPLETE-VINTAGE YEARS ONLY (scripts/calibration_verdict.score_fuelmix, year >= PRELIM_923_FROM_YEAR=2025): every 2025 fossil class is SKIPPED (recorded, not gated, never a silent pass; the raw model-actual gap is kept only as a report-only vintage_gap_twh annotation), so CC_REGULAR's +6.15 TWh is no longer scored as a per-class miss. The 2025 gas family is still governed by C2's EIA-930 grid reconcile. 2023/2024 (complete 923) keep the full per-class PASS/FAIL gate. This supersedes the run154-as-registered diagnosis (which attributed the +6.15 to freed-CT over-absorption into Hidalgo/Colorado Bend CCs with root-cause pending); the 930-vs-923 vintage check shows the freed CT energy did NOT create a real gas surplus - the model's gas total is correct vs 930. (2) Permian Basin (3494) and Ector County (58471) still over-run with a residual cheap-hour magnet in 2024 (the deep-gas year, dispatch r vs load -0.44/-0.38); in 2025 (expensive West gas) they land near real CF (398/450 vs 456/642 GWh). The 2024 magnet is the remainder a within-West gas shape cannot close at the physical delivered floor - the West CTs serve large local load and are NOT transmission-closable (West export uses ~2 of 10 GW TTC; the Far_West split was previously built and rejected). (3) Laredo's modeled HR (9.16) is low for a GT peaker - a per-unit EIA-860 data item, now immaterial since the zone fix idles it correctly (56 vs 52 GWh).
